definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese sitting posture of kneeling with legs folded underneath, sitting on one's heels. Considered the most formal way to sit on tatami.

examples.japanese: {正座|せいざ}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{待|ま}っていた→待つ：00469_matsu⟧。
examples.english: I was waiting in formal sitting position.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧{正座|せいざ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痺|しび}れる→痺れる：06814_shibireru⟧。
examples.english: Your legs go numb if you sit in seiza for a long time.

examples.japanese: ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{正座|せいざ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{基本|きほん}→基本：00226_kihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{姿勢|しせい}→姿勢：00371_shisei⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In the tea ceremony, seiza is considered the standard posture.

notes:
WRITING:
⟦{正|せい}→正：09511_sei⟧ (correct/proper) + ⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧ (sitting). Literally "correct sitting."

USAGE:
{正座|せいざ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ is the verb form (to sit in seiza). This posture is expected in formal settings like ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧ (tea ceremony), ⟦{書道|しょどう}→書道：04178_shodou⟧ (calligraphy), and ⟦{武道|ぶどう}→武道：09640_budou⟧ (martial arts), as well as at funerals and formal gatherings on ⟦{畳|たたみ}→畳：02224_tatami⟧.

Many modern Japanese people find {正座|せいざ} uncomfortable for extended periods, and it is common for legs to fall asleep (⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痺|しび}れる→痺れる：06814_shibireru⟧).

NOTE ON HOMOPHONES:
Do not confuse with ⟦{星座|せいざ}→星座：06313_seiza⟧ (constellation), which has the same reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正座|せいざ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to sit in seiza
- {正座|せいざ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{崩|くず}す→崩す：03919_kuzusu⟧: to shift out of seiza into a more relaxed position
- ⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{痺|しび}れる→痺れる：06814_shibireru⟧: legs go numb (from seiza)
